newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FCC extends broadcast licenses terms.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FCC extends broadcast licenses terms.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Communications Commission said Friday it had extended the license terms that are awarded to television and radio stations to eight years. The current maximums are five and seven years for different categories of broadcasters.
The FCC said it took the regulatory action to implement a section of the 1996 Telecommunications Act.
"The lengthened license terms will reduce the burden to broadcasters seeking periodic renewal of their licenses and can allow the competitive marketplace to operate more efficiently," the FCC said.
